Since the class is package-private, my test needs to live in the same package, com.google.javascript.jscomp, and since it implements NodeTraversal.ScopedCallback, I need to account for its dependency on intern.

I'm reasoning through classpath concerns—NodeTraversal, Scope, NodeUtil, and AbstractCompiler are jscomp-internal classes rather than part of the rhino jar, but since Defects4J compiles tests against the full project source, these should be available implicitly even though they aren't explicitly listed as jars.

So I could actually use the real Compiler and NodeTraversal classes to write an integration-style test: parse a JS snippet into an AST, run NodeTraversal.traverse with MakeDeclaredNamesUnique, and check how variable names get rewritten as a result.

Since I don't have JUnit4's CompilerTestCase available, I need to build this test using the Compiler class directly instead, parsing the source string and setting up the traversal manually.
